- The speaker remains persistently drawn to an aloof person who repeatedly avoids intimacy and rendezvous.
- This unfulfilled attraction diminishes the speaker’s enjoyment of ordinary pleasures and disrupts their professional ambitions.
- Fleeting glances and remembered encounters sustain an unresolved romantic narrative filled with regret over missed chances.
- The speaker longs to believe the obsession is mutual, despite repeated signs of the other person’s withdrawal.

prompts.L4:
Please expand the following two-sentence summary into a complete text:

An unrequited lover uses elaborate French phrases and vivid urban memories to chronicle obsessive longing, missed encounters, and the disruption of everyday ambitions. Despite repeated rejection and the apparent impossibility of fulfillment, the speaker remains watchful and hopeful, revealing desire’s power to sustain an endless, self-defeating pursuit.
prompts.L5:
Please write a text about the following topic:

Keywords: Though, The, Each

outputs.L1:
Though it is all too clear how unimpressed you are by a cri de cœur—and that, from your perspective, wafting away unhugged is de rigueur whenever I scheme to rendezvous with you—I remain a restless entrepreneur. The thought of you transforms my favorite main dishes into mere hors d’œuvres. My addiction to the tingling you induce is a fait accompli.

Each drifting day is another page in the secret book whose dénouement never arrives, while your fleeting glances bind me to this unfinishable roman à clef. The notion that some remembered moment at a party or picnic was my sole, forever-lost chance to touch you must surely be a cul-de-sac.

Whenever my plans for a prudent career try to stand, the memory of your voice administers the coup de grâce, and my mélange of bright ideas becomes a mere potpourri. How I would love to believe that this dance is a folie à deux.

The way you stride across Memorial Drive is a tour de force, but glimpses across traffic make for a paper-thin raison d’être. Your recent exit is implicit in many a mise-en-scène. It is as though you heard me approaching for a tête-à-tête, then slipped into the elevator in your tall boots and with your sangfroid intact.

Always, you get to reculer, while I never seem to mieux sauter. Still, I will keep an eye out for you on every rez-de-chaussée.
outputs.L2:
You may have little patience for heartfelt pleas, and from where you stand, drifting off without an embrace seems to be the required outcome of every plan I make to meet you. Even so, I remain an agitated schemer. Merely thinking of you reduces the meals I love most to insignificant appetizers. The thrill you awaken in me has already become an irreversible dependence.

Every passing day adds another leaf to a hidden volume that never reaches its ending, while your momentary looks trap me inside a coded novel that cannot be completed. I refuse to accept that some recollected instant at a gathering or picnic represented my one vanished opportunity to touch you; that belief must lead nowhere.

Whenever my designs for a sensible profession begin to take shape, the memory of your voice delivers the fatal blow, turning my blend of promising notions into a random assortment. I wish I could imagine that the two of us share the same madness.

Watching you cross Memorial Drive is a masterful spectacle, yet catching sight of you through moving traffic offers only the flimsiest reason to exist. Your latest departure seems embedded in scene after scene. It feels as though you sensed that I was coming for a private conversation, then calmly escaped into the elevator in your high boots. You are always the one able to step back before making a better leap, while I never manage the same maneuver.

Nevertheless, I will continue searching for you on every ground floor.
outputs.L3:
The speaker remains persistently attracted to an aloof and elusive person who repeatedly resists intimacy and avoids opportunities for meaningful encounters. This unfulfilled desire gradually overshadows the speaker’s daily life, diminishing the pleasure found in ordinary experiences and interfering with professional ambitions. Fleeting glances, brief meetings, and vivid memories keep the attachment alive, creating an unresolved romantic narrative shaped by longing and regret over missed opportunities.

Despite clear signs of withdrawal, the speaker wants to believe that the attraction may be mutual. This hope allows the obsession to endure, even when the other person’s behavior suggests distance or rejection. Each departure therefore feels painful but not final. After the latest separation, the speaker continues to imagine another chance encounter, remaining caught between the evidence of emotional unavailability and the persistent hope that the relationship might still be renewed.
outputs.L4:
The speaker recounts an unrequited passion through ornate French expressions and sharply rendered memories of city life. Streets, cafés, windows, stations, and passing crowds become charged with the possibility of seeing the beloved again. Every ordinary outing turns into a search, while every remembered glance or missed meeting is examined for hidden meaning. The lover’s absence is therefore never complete: imagination continually restores the beloved to the urban landscape, transforming chance encounters into promises and disappointments into material for further hope.

This fixation gradually unsettles the speaker’s practical life. Work, plans, and personal ambitions lose their urgency because desire occupies the attention that everyday responsibilities require. Although rejection has been repeated and fulfillment appears impossible, the speaker cannot accept a definitive ending. Instead, remaining watchful becomes a way of preserving the attachment. Hope survives not because circumstances justify it, but because longing has become sustaining in itself. The pursuit is endless and self-defeating, yet it gives shape and intensity to the speaker’s world, demonstrating how desire can endure by feeding on the very distance and denial that prevent it from being satisfied.
outputs.L5: **Though the path was uncertain, each step carried hope. The journey demanded patience, and each challenge offered a lesson. Though success seemed distant, the traveler continued, believing that each new day brought another chance to move forward.**

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a surreal, unrequited-love prose poem about obsessively missing an aloof woman, using many French loanwords and expressions.
counterfactuals.output:
I miss you with the mauvais goût of a chandelier burning at noon, extravagant and useless. Every morning, the city opens its gray pâtisserie of hours, and I choose the same stale éclair: your absence, glazed with déjà vu. I eat it slowly. I call it breakfast. I call it amour fou.

You, meanwhile, remain très chic in the penthouse of indifference, lifting one eyebrow like a drawbridge. Your silence has savoir-faire. It enters a room before you do, orders champagne, and leaves no pourboire. Once, you said *à bientôt* beneath a red awning, and I have lived ever since inside those two words, furnished them with velvet, hung mirrors in their corridor, trained white moths to pronounce your name.

Quelle catastrophe: the moon has become your cold profile. The Seine flows through my apartment at midnight, carrying little bateaux-mouches filled with copies of you—each one aloof, each one wearing the same black gloves, each one turning away at the precise moment I begin my confession. I pursue them in a papier-mâché gondola, crying *revenez*, but the river spills into the wardrobe, and all my coats wake up smelling of winter and Chanel.

I practice nonchalance in the mirror. *Comme ci, comme ça*, I tell my reflection, while behind me the wallpaper grows your eyes. I attempt esprit, ennui, a certain je ne sais quoi. I smoke imaginary Gauloises with the aplomb of a doomed marquis. But my heart is a gauche little concierge who keeps your key beneath his tongue.

At cafés, I reserve a chair for your ghost. The garçon knows our tableau: one coffee, two cups, no rendez-vous. Pigeons gather like critics. They disapprove of my mise-en-scène, my sentimental faux pas, the ridiculous bouquet of blue roses sweating beside your empty place. *C’est la vie*, they coo, with brutal joie de vivre.

But it is not la vie. It is limbo with good lighting.

At night, I inventory the minutiae: the coup de grâce of your shrug, the cool ballet of your hands, the bon mot you gave another man and never knew I overheard. I remember how you looked through me—not cruelly, no, but with perfect sang-froid, as though I were a window overlooking nothing. That nothing has become my entire paysage.

Mon Dieu, how elegantly you do not love me.

Still, I send no letter. I preserve my dignity like a useless hors d’œuvre beneath glass. I only lie awake while the ceiling lowers itself, centimeter by centimeter, until the room becomes a small white envelope. Inside it, I am the unsent message. Inside me, your name repeats in cursive, obsessive and illegible.

And somewhere you are sleeping, peut-être, without dreaming of me at all.

Voilà the miracle. Voilà the wound.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose a single-paragraph monologue in which a restless entrepreneur longs for someone who repeatedly evades him, ending with “rez-de-chaussée.”
counterfactuals.output: I have launched companies from napkin sketches, coaxed fortunes out of sleepless nights, and crossed oceans before breakfast because stillness feels too much like surrender, yet I cannot close the distance between us: every message arrives after you have left, every train pulls away with your silhouette behind the glass, every crowded room holds the echo of your almost-laughter. I know how to pursue markets, investors, impossible deadlines—but not you, who turns each encounter into a vanishing act. So I keep moving, pitching, building, pretending ambition is enough, while secretly hoping that one evening I will race to your building before you disappear again and find you waiting, at last, on the rez-de-chaussée.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Create an experimental love poem set around Memorial Drive, elevators, parties, and fleeting encounters. Incorporate phrases such as cri de cœur, de rigueur, fait accompli, coup de grâce, folie à deux, and tête-à-tête.
counterfactuals.output:
**MEMORIAL DRIVE, AFTER MIDNIGHT**

Along Memorial Drive, the river  
wears the city like a borrowed dress—  
sequins of traffic, black silk,  
a moon pinned crooked at the shoulder.

At the party, everyone is becoming  
someone else. Champagne: *de rigueur*.  
Laughter rises through the rooms  
like an elevator with no floor numbers.

You step in.  
I step in.  
The doors close—

our small *tête-à-tête*  
between Lobby and 14,  
your hand near mine,  
not touching: a *cri de cœur*  
spoken fluently by distance.

Then the bell.  
Then strangers.  
Then music doing its beautiful damage.

We orbit the kitchen, the balcony,  
the host whose name neither of us remembers.  
By two a.m., desire is a *fait accompli*:  
your coat over my shoulders,  
my pulse signing for it.

Outside, Memorial Drive keeps moving—  
headlights loosening in the rain,  
the Charles holding every reflection  
for one second, then none.

Call it *folie à deux*:  
we believe the night has chosen us.  
We believe the elevator is still rising.  
We believe every party has a secret room  
where no one leaves.

But morning—precise *coup de grâce*—  
finds your cab already turning,  
your face briefly framed in glass,

and me on the curb,  
loving the red taillights  
for carrying you away,  
loving them less  
with every disappearing mile.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a witty, melancholy piece of poetic prose about romantic obsession, career distractions, and missed chances, densely peppered with French terms commonly used in English.
counterfactuals.output:
She was my idée fixe, though I preferred to call her a passing liaison, the way one calls a hurricane “weather.” I cultivated nonchalance with great savoir-faire: a shrug here, a bon mot there, the occasional cigarette held like an alibi. Meanwhile, every café became our café, every déjà vu a communiqué from fate, and every woman in a red coat an understudy in the grand ballet of my despair.

My career was the perfect faute de mieux. I pursued promotions with élan, accepted each new portfolio as though ambition were an aperitif, and became, by degrees, the enfant terrible of quarterly forecasts. My résumé acquired cachet; my apartment acquired objets d’art; my soul acquired office hours. Colleagues praised my sang-froid while I answered her imaginary letters between meetings. C’est la vie, I told myself, mistaking cliché for closure.

Once, in a hotel lobby in Lyon—or perhaps it was merely a lobby decorated to suggest Lyon—I saw her beside a ficus, radiant and slightly bored. The moment had mise-en-scène, chiaroscuro, even a discreet concierge. All it lacked was courage. I could have crossed the room. I could have said her name. Instead, I checked my agenda, that petty bourgeois oracle, and hurried toward a conference call about “synergy.”

Years later, I learned she had waited there for twenty minutes.

Voilà: the whole tragicomic oeuvre. Love offered me a rendezvous; I sent regrets. Opportunity knocked; I was on mute. Now I enjoy a certain prestige, a generous pension, and the exquisite ennui of a man who got everything except the point.

Sometimes, at dusk, I order a digestif and toast the coup de foudre that never quite struck. The waiter says, “À votre santé.”

“Merci,” I reply.

But of course, it is far too late for health.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Produce a stream-of-consciousness lament addressed to an unattainable lover in tall boots, mixing business imagery, literary metaphors, and escalating French expressions without translating them.
counterfactuals.output:
You in the tall boots, clicking through my sleep like a hostile takeover—how did you acquire every corridor, every trembling subsidiary of the heart, without signing once, without even glancing at the fine print? I had forecasts. I had safeguards. I had a little ledger where desire was entered in pencil and risk in red, but then you crossed the room and the whole quarter collapsed, margins bleeding into moonlight, my careful empire reduced to a footnote in a novel nobody finishes.

Ah, toi—distant as a lighthouse in some unwritten Brontë storm, severe as a semicolon in Flaubert, you stand there while I pitch my ruin in slides: first, the market opportunity; second, the tragic flaw; third, the projected eternity of your absence. You nod as if sorrow were billable, as if I could invoice you for every night your boots echo down the marble staircase of my imagination.

Mon cœur, ma belle, écoute—no, don’t; if you listened, the metaphor might become flesh, and flesh is where every enterprise discovers its liabilities. Better to remain impossible, a premium brand of catastrophe, the dark quotation at the beginning of my chapter. Still, I revise the proposal. I sweeten the terms. I offer controlling interest in my silence, preferred shares in my longing, a seat forever vacant at the board.

Mais pourquoi, pourquoi toujours toi? Your heels strike midnight into smaller midnights. Your shadow audits me. Every secret fails compliance. I am overleveraged in memory, insolvent in hope, and yet I keep expanding operations—new branches of grief, new offices in cities where you have never been, each one furnished with a desk, a lamp, and those boots approaching but never arriving.

Mon amour impossible, mon désastre magnifique, je t’en supplie—walk past me again, slowly, cruelly, so I may mistake the sound for destiny. Let me be your unread letter, your abandoned prospectus, your minor character waiting faithfully in the rain while the great plot carries you elsewhere.

Oh là là, non, non, non—c’est fini, c’est impossible, c’est une folie sans fin—and still I sign at the bottom, still I initial every page, still I whisper oui beneath the stamp of rejection, oui beneath the falling stock, oui as the library burns, oui, oui, jusqu’au vertige, jusqu’à la ruine, jusqu’à ce que même la nuit déclare faillite.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
